questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a vocal form of Hindustani classical music?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Pakhawaj**__ is not a vocal form of Hindustani classical music. It is a two-headed drum which is barrel-shaped, also known as mridang.
 
• Tarana, Drupad, Khyal, and Dhamar are major vocal forms of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Hindustani classical music originated in 12th century CE.
 
• The music has 7 basic notes and 5 interspersed half-notes, which result in a 12-note scale.

questions.question: Who was the first woman judge of the Delhi High Court?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Leila Seth**__ was the first woman judge of the Delhi High Court.
 
• She was also the first woman to become Chief Justice of a High Court of a state on 5 August 1991.
 
• Anna Chandi was the first female judge of India.
 
• Sujata Manohar is a retired judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• Ruma Pal is a former Supreme Court judge in India.

questions.question: The Khajuraho Temples are located in the state of ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Khajuraho Temples are located in the state of **Madhya Pradesh,**__ in Chhatarpur district.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandela dynasty in the year 950-1050.
 
• It was added in UNESCO sites in 1986.

questions.question: Which one of the following was NOT a condition laid down in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?

options.text: Withdrawal of tax on khadi production
Removal of salt tax; allowing to produce, trade and sell legally
The Indian National Congress should stop the civil disobedience movement
Participation in the Round Table Conference by the Indian National Congress

questions.solution:
__
 
• The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**__ was an agreement signed between Lord Irwin and Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It __**conditions**__ were:
 
• Removal of salt tax; allowing to produce, trade and sell legally
 
• The Indian National Congress should stop the civil disobedience movement
 
• Participation in the Round Table Conference by the Indian National Congress
 
• Withdrawal of ordinances issued by the Indian government
 
• Release of prisoners who were arrested for taking part in the Salt March

questions.question: The ________ was a group of seven Members of Parliament from the United Kingdom, constituted to suggest constitutional reforms for British India.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The** Simon Commission(1927)**__ was a group of seven Members of Parliament from the United Kingdom, constituted to suggest constitutional reforms for British India. 
 
• Sir John Simon was its chairman.
 
• A protest against it was led by nationalist Lala Lajpat Rai in Lahore, during which he died because of his injuries in 1928.
 
• The Sargent scheme was a 1944 memorandum prepared by the British-run Government of India. It outlined the future development of literacy and education in India.
 
• The McGovern–Fraser Commission was created by the Democratic National Committee (DNC) in response to the Democratic National Convention 1968.
 
• Hunter Commission,1882, was the first education commission in the history of modern India.

questions.question: Bariatric surgery makes changes to a person's ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Bariatric surgery**__ makes changes to a person's digestive system.
 
• It is also known as gastric bypass surgery.
 
• It helps a person lose weight by changing how mall intestine and stomach handle the food one eats.
 
• Thoracotomy is a surgery for the lungs.
 
• Turbinectomy is a surgery for the nasal passage.
 
• Bypass surgery is a surgery for the heart.

questions.question: ________ is the largest river island in the world.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Majuli**__ is the largest river island in the world.
 
• It is situated in Assam on the Brahmaputra river.
 
• It is spread across an area of 880 sq km and is inhabited by tribes such as Deori and Mising.
 
• The Guinness World Records has declared the Majuli island as the largest river island in the world, toppling Marajo in Brazil to clinch the record.

questions.question: Varkala, Chowara, Chavakkad and Nattika are beaches in the state of ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Varkala, Chowara, Chavakkad and Nattika are beaches in the state of **Kerala.**__
 
• Kerala is a popular tourist destination in India.
 
• Other famous places of Kerala include Ponmudi, Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary, Idukki Dam, etc.

questions.question: The National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises meets once every ________ months in a year.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The National Board for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises meets once every **6__ **months in a year.
 
• It was established on 15 May 2007, having 47 members.
 
• It is responsible for examining the factors affecting the development and promotion of MSMEs.
 
• It also gives advice to the Central government about the use of funds constituted in Section 12.

questions.question: Which of the following acid is found in Apple?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Malic**__ acid is found in apples.
 
• It is a dicarboxylic acid which is also present in grapes, wine, and rhubarb.
 
• It imparts a tart taste to a food.
 
• Formic acid is found in ants.

questions.question: ________ was the first and only Muslim woman to ever sit on the throne of Delhi.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Razia Sultan**__ was the first and the only Muslim woman to ever sit on the throne of Delhi.
 
• She was appointed by Iltutmish.
 
• She served as the Sultan of Delhi from 10 October 1236- 14 October 1240.
 
• Shajar Al Durr was an Egyptian ruler.
 
• Gevher Nesibe was the princess of Sultanate of Rum.
 
• Fatima Al Fihri was an Arab Musli woman who founded the oldest existing educational institution in the world.

questions.question: The Banking Regulation Act was passed in India in ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Banking Regulation Act was passed in India in the year **1949**__.
 
• The act regulates all the banking firms in India.
 
• It came into effect on 16 March 1949 and was applicable in Jammu and Kashmir from 1956.

questions.question: What is India's rank in 2019 World Happiness Report?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Indian ranked **140th**__ in 2019 World Happiness Report, released in March 2019.
 
• Finland topped the ranking for the second consecutive year.
 
• India dropped down by 7 places. It was at 133rd position in 2018.
 
• Pakistan stood at 67th, while China at 93rd position.
 
• The report ranks countries on the basis of national happiness.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Mandhan Yojana was launched by ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Mandhan Yojana was launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**__ in March 2019 in Ahmedabad for unorganized sector workers.
 
• The scheme ensures old age protection with a monthly pension of Rs. 3000 for people aged 60 years and above.
 
• Workers whose monthly income is less than or equal to Rs.15000/month will benefit from this scheme.
 
• The maximum yearly contribution is Rs.2400, that is, Rs. 200 per month.

questions.question: ________ is the oldest golf course outside the United Kingdom.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Royal Calcutta Golf Club, Kolkata**__ is the oldest golf course outside the United Kingdom.
 
• It was established in the year 1829.
 
• It is also the second-oldest club outside Scotland.
 
• The Royal Blackheath in London is the oldest one outside Scotland, which was established in the year 1776.

questions.question: The Indian Passport was ranked ________ in the 'Global Passport Index Report 2019'.
questions.solution:
__

questions.question: Article ________ of the Constitution of India gives the Election Commission the power to supervise elections to the Parliament and state legislatures.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Article 324**__ of the Indian Constitution gives the Election Commission the power to supervise elections to the Parliament and state legislatures.
 
• Article 342 deals with Scheduled Tribes in India.
 
• Article 314 has been repealed.
 
• Article 341 deals with Scheduled Castes of India.

questions.question: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended by ________.

options.text: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
The Commission for Weights and Measures

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. __Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)__.

 
• **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
 
• MSP is a price set by the Indian government at which it purchases crops directly from the farmer.
 
• It is an important part of the agricultural policy of India.
 
• **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** is a form of market intervention by the Government of India to insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a symptom of Wilson's disease?

options.text: Fluid build-up in the legs or abdomen
Problems with speech, swallowing or physical coordination

questions.solution:
__
 
• **Wilson's disease**__ is a disorder which causes accumulation of copper in the brain, liver and other organs.
 
• Its symptoms include:
 
• Fluid build-up in the legs or abdomen
 
• Problems with speech, swallowing or physical coordination
 
• Uncontrolled movements or muscle stiffness
 
• Fatigue, lack of appetite
 
• Yellowing of skin

questions.question: During photosynthesis, green plants use energy from sunlight to synthesise ________ from carbon dioxide and water.
questions.solution:
__
 
• During photosynthesis, green plants use energy from sunlight to synthesise **glucose**__ from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• Photosynthesis is a process that plants and other organisms use to convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• Glucose, fructose, sucrose and galactose are all forms of simple sugar.

questions.solution:
__
 
• **Aditi Ashok**__ became the first Indian golfer to win on the 'Ladies European Tour' in 2016.
 
• She is an 18-year old golfer.
